title: The insult no one took
told: a story from the Pali Canon

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? when someone says something unkind to you, what usually happens to it?
options: then you’re in good company. this story is for you.
oh, i know that one. listen to this.
that’s a real gift. here’s where it comes from.

steps.line: Near the city of Rajagaha, in a quiet bamboo grove, the Buddha was staying with his monks.
A man named Bharadvaja stormed in. Someone from his own clan had just become a monk, and he was furious.
He shouted insult after insult at the Buddha. The Buddha listened, calm, and waited.

steps.q: When the shouting stops, what does the Buddha do?
o: He stays silent until the man is done
He asks the man about his house guests
He tells him anger only hurts himself
steps.why: A question, not a comeback. And it’s about something homely: food, and guests.

steps.line: “Do friends and guests ever come to your house?” the Buddha asked. “Sometimes.” “And do you offer them food?” “Sometimes, yes.”

steps.q: “And if your guests don’t eat it,” the Buddha asks, “whose food is it then?” What do you think Bharadvaja answers?
o: “Then we give it to the dogs.”
steps.why: “Then it’s ours,” he says, and walks right into it. In the Pali text (SN 7.2) the Buddha replies: you’ve served me abuse I won’t take, so it’s all yours, brahmin.

steps.line: “In the same way,” said the Buddha, “I don’t accept your insults. So they all belong to you.”

steps.q: A coworker snaps at you. What would “not accepting it,” the Buddha’s way, look like?
o: Smiling and acting like it’s fine
Not hitting back or replaying it
steps.why: It isn’t pretending or putting on a brave face. You let the words stay with the one who said them, and choose your own next action.

steps.q: The Buddha goes on: when someone insults you and you insult back, what are you doing, in his picture?
o: Cooking a meal of your own
steps.why: In the old text, trading insults is “dining together, sharing the meal.” Handing it back is what the Buddha does instead.

steps.line: They talked on, and Bharadvaja’s anger cooled. The old text says he soon asked to become a monk himself.

steps.q: The man who stormed in to shout became a monk. What does the old text say happened after that?
o: He went home to make peace with his clan
He became fully awakened, an arahant
He became the Buddha’s chief helper
steps.why: The text ends: “And the Venerable Bharadvaja became one of the arahants.” The angriest man in the grove went all the way.

say: in buddhism, karma just means action. and the buddha said the heart of it is intention: what you mean as you act.
bharadvaja’s anger was his seed to grow, and the buddha’s calm was his. that’s why many buddhists chant: i am the owner of my actions, heir to my actions.

steps.q: He came to be remembered as Akkosaka Bharadvaja. From this story, what do you think Akkosaka means?
steps.why: Akkosaka comes from akkosa, “insult” or “abuse.” The name kept his old habit, even after he changed.

today.say: today, if a sharp word comes your way, picture it as a dish set in front of you. you don’t have to pick it up. and before you answer, notice what you mean.
options: that’s karma at its root: choosing what you mean.
it is. the buddha’s calm took practice too. one try counts.

tomorrow.title: The monk who bowed to everyone
tomorrow.line: he bowed to every person he met, even the ones who threw stones.

card.from: a story from the Pali Canon
card.keepWhy: What you mean is what you grow.
sources: Akkosa Sutta, Samyutta Nikaya 7.2: the abusive brahmin Bharadvaja, the guests and the food, “it all belongs to you”; set in the Bamboo Grove, Squirrels’ Sanctuary, Rajagaha
Nibbedhika Sutta, Anguttara Nikaya 6.63: “intention is what I call kamma”
Upajjhatthana Sutta, Anguttara Nikaya 5.57: “owner of my actions, heir to my actions”
Samuddaka Sutta, Samyutta Nikaya 11.10: as the seed is sown, so is the fruit
check: The sutta says a brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan had gone forth; the commentary makes him his brother. The lesson says “someone from his own clan.”
